summary: Frontend E2E for handling times, shipment delay alerts and packing slips, run on the preview URL at desktop 1920 and mobile 390. Backend pytest was not re-run, as requested. Seeded with tests/seed_phase08_ui.py plus a new helper, tests/seed_iter10_handling.py (accepts B, creates and accepts a pickup order, forces deadlines into the past and runs the handling-alerts cron). VERIFIED: (1) Vendor shipping options: a new delivery option with blank days defaults to 3, a pickup option with 2 days saves, days=40 is rejected with 'Handling time must be between 1 and 10 business days.', and editing the row inline (method-days-{id}) out of range shows an error toast while 4 saves and persists after reload. (2) Checkout shows 'Ships within 3/4 business days after the seller accepts' and 'Ready for pickup within 2 business days after the seller accepts' per option (checkout-handling-{slug}-{id}). (3) Customer order detail: pending shows 'Ships within 3 business days after the seller accepts.', accepted ship shows 'Expected to ship by Tue, Oct 27' (Thu + 3 business days, correct), accepted pickup shows 'Expected ready for pickup by Mon, Oct 26' (correct). Overdue states show late wording in clay colour: ship 'running late; we've asked the seller to ship right away', pickup 'preparation is running late'. The timeline shows 'Pickup preparation is taking longer than expected'. (4) Vendor /vendor/orders: no deadline before Accept; after Accept 'Ship by Tue, Oct 27'; pickup overdue shows 'Ready for pickup by Thu, Oct 22 — overdue'; after the admin extension it shows 'Ship by Mon, Oct 26 (extended)'. The order-level slip download returns a valid 1-page US Letter PDF (612x792). The Print button opens a new tab. Partial shipment exposes slip-download/print-{shipmentId}, and that PDF lists only the package items with 'Package: USPS <tracking>'. The PDF text has the AfroVending brand, www.afrovending.com, info@afrovending.com, order number and date, vendor, ship-to address, item, SKU, quantity and the return instruction, with no '$' or prices. Vendor B gets 404 on vendor A's slip. (5) The cron created exactly one overdue_customer and one overdue_vendor notification_log per suborder. (6) Admin /admin/fulfillment: all new config fields and toggles load with the defaults. Default=15 (outside 1–10) gives an error toast; valid changes (default 4, reminder 12, non-business days, toggle off) persist after reload; a bad date string gives an error toast. The config was restored to defaults. The overdue list shows both orders with 'shipment' and 'pickup preparation' wording. Extend is disabled when the reason is under 5 characters; after a valid extension the toast shows, the order leaves the list and the deadline moves 2 business days (Thu -> Mon, weekend skipped). (7) Mobile 390: no horizontal page overflow on vendor orders (the tabs row scrolls inside its own container) or on admin fulfillment. Every requested flow passed; only minor and UX issues were found.

minor.issue: The notification_log record is written before the email is sent, and try_send failures are swallowed. During this run, backend.err.log showed several 'Email send failed: 429 rate_limited' from Resend at the moment the cron fired. Those customer/vendor overdue emails are now marked sent and will never be retried. Store the send result and retry failed ones (e.g. status=failed + retry on the next run), or throttle sends.

HANDLING_ACTIVE = (accepted, processing). A partially_shipped suborder whose remaining items are never shipped gets no reminder, no overdue alert, no admin listing and no deadline display, on either the vendor or the customer side. Decide whether partial shipment should satisfy the deadline; if not, include partially_shipped.

Validation messages come through with the raw Pydantic prefix: 'Value error, Default handling time must sit between the minimum and maximum.' and 'Value error, Non-business days must look like 2026-12-25.'. Strip the 'Value error, ' prefix in the error handler.

The extension is added to the old (possibly long-past) deadline. If it is still in the past, overdue is reset to False and the next cron run sends a second apology email under the new deadline tag. Consider extending from max(now, deadline) or warning the admin.

ui_bugs.issue: The frontend ignores the backend Content-Disposition filename. Both the order-level and the per-shipment slip download as 'packing-slip-{order_number}.pdf' (the backend sends ...-{tracking}.pdf), and the two buttons share the same label 'Download packing slip' on the same row. Use the header filename and label the shipment one 'Slip for this package'. Object URLs are never revoked.

window.open is called after an await (the blob fetch), so strict popup blockers (Safari, Firefox) may block it, and w.addEventListener('load', print) often doesn't fire for PDF viewer tabs. Consider a hidden iframe print, or open the window synchronously before the fetch.
After an out-of-range edit fails, the input keeps the invalid value (15) instead of reverting to the saved value, so the UI is out of sync with the server.
No singular form: '1 business days' when handling_days=1. Checkout already handles this.

issues: The new-option placeholder 'Handling days (3)' is truncated to 'Handling days (3' in the w-36 input, and it hardcodes 3 instead of the admin default.
The page heading still reads 'Cancellations & returns' although it now holds handling config and overdue orders.
Overdue rows lack how long the order has been overdue, the customer, any link to the order and the escalation status; each row starts with a stray '·'.

action_items: Make overdue/reminder notifications retry on email failure (429 seen in logs) instead of marking them sent before delivery
Decide on and handle deadlines for partially_shipped suborders (alerts, admin overdue list, deadline display)
Strip the 'Value error, ' prefix from config validation toasts
Packing slip: use the backend filename, give the per-shipment button a distinct label, make Print robust (iframe or synchronous window.open), revoke object URLs
Revert method-days input on save failure; fix '1 business days' pluralisation on OrderDetailPage
Admin overdue list: show overdue duration, customer and an order link; rename the page heading
critical_code_review_comments: fulfillment.handling_alerts: _once() inserts into notification_log before notify_*; with try_send swallowing errors, failed emails are lost permanently.
HANDLING_ACTIVE excludes partially_shipped, so partially fulfilled orders silently drop out of SLA tracking.
handling_alerts iterates every active vendor order on each run and sends notifications sequentially; fine for an MVP, but add an index on (status, handling.deadline_at) and batch the work.
VendorOrdersPage openSlip: URL.createObjectURL is never revoked, and the anchor is not appended to the DOM (works in Chrome).

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows pass; 4 low-priority UI bugs, plus design and minor backend notes

test_credentials: Super admin from /app/memory/test_credentials.md worked. Runtime TEST8UI_ users (delivered+t8ui*@resend.dev / TestPass12345) were created and deleted.
seed_data_creation: Seeded 2 vendors, 2 products, 3 shipping methods, a buyer, 2 paid orders (4 vendor_orders), 1 shipment and notification_log records. All were deleted with seed_phase08_ui cleanup, plus notification_log, cron_runs, and the 22 Stripe webhook_events and 72 audit_logs created by this run. platform_settings fulfillment.config is at defaults (3/1/10/24/48, all toggles true, return 14, response 48, non_business_days []). Final: users=1, vendors/orders/vendor_orders/shipments/notification_log/shipping_methods=0. 92 older webhook_events from earlier runs were left untouched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run seed: cd /app/backend && PYTHONPATH=/app/backend python -m tests.seed_phase08_ui seed. Then python -m tests.seed_iter10_handling prep (B accept, pickup order via vendor A's pickup method, needs vendor A to already have a pickup method created in the UI), then 'overdue' (deadlines set to now-2h, cron run), then 'logs'. Clean up with seed_phase08_ui cleanup, and delete notification_log by vendor_order_id first. The server clock is in Oct 2026. Not tested in the UI: the 24h reminder and 48h admin escalation (covered by pytest), and print dialog content.
